affected_docs.why: The only page this task's author edits. `## Installing` runs lines 91-108 and carries a four-step numbered procedure (steps at 97, 98, 102, 106) on a page whose frontmatter declares `type: platform-overview` at line 4; that is the defect wiki/page-types.md:243-245 names. Step 4 at line 108 carries the measured RTF of 0.96, which the corpus publishes nowhere else, so it needs a destination in a surviving section. `## What installing gives you` ends at lines 87-89 with a single sentence on Settings > Connection, and doc_graph.py reports install-macos.md's `## Starting and stopping the backend` as overlapping this exact section at 0.39, which is where the salvage from wiki/install-macos.md:118-126 lands. `## Status and limitations` is touched whether or not the author intends it: its bullet at lines 128-129 reads 'first launch needs the right-click-Open step above', and 'above' is step 2 of the section being removed, so the removal orphans that back-reference.

sources_of_truth.covers: What the Settings pane actually offers. Line 238 is the section labelled Connection; line 271 is a Row labelled The house inside it; line 272 is the shipped hint, 'The backend on this machine: the mind, the voice, and the ears. Stopping it frees their memory; starting it brings them back without relaunching Hearth.'; lines 274-286 render running with a process count, stopped, or unknown; the controls are Start (288), Stop (291) and Restart (297); lines 302-312 name each failed process and its detail. Line 90 gates the whole row on no server address being set and an install root existing. This settles every behavioural claim in the salvage passage.

What Stop does. stop() takes the House out of state, flushes sessions through the gateway port, sets the stopping flag, kills every managed child and clears them, then drops the kill-on-close job handle which reaps anything missed, llama-server included. The app itself is not exited. That is why stopping frees the memory the model and voice hold while Hearth stays open.

The open-and-quit lifecycle. App.tsx starts the house behind a boot overlay when a validated local install is found at launch; lib.rs stops it on the tray Quit item (73-76) and on RunEvent::Exit (96-98). Lines 83-89 are the countercase no macOS page states: a window close hides the window and prevents the close, so the backend keeps running, and Quit lives in the tray.

That wiki/raw/ genuinely never publishes. EXCLUDE_DIRS is set to raw at line 46 and applied at 69-70 to skip any page whose first path part is in it; the module docstring at 29-31 states the exclusion is deliberate. Corroborated by scripts/lint_wiki.py:31,83-88,293-294. This settles the premise that the RTF number has no other published home.

What RTF means in this product: generation seconds divided by seconds of audio, logged per synthesis at line 168, with the diffusion-step count named as the latency lever. It defines the metric but asserts no Mac measurement; the figures at 43-44 are for a shared 4080.

The run record that produced the number. Written 2026-08-07 on an 8 GB M2 Air running macOS 27, it states that synthesis measured RTF 0.961 on a real tool-grounded reply, faster than realtime, on the smallest machine the product supports. It is the only origin the corpus has for the published 0.96, and it never publishes.

The passage being copied. `## Starting and stopping the backend` states that Hearth starts its backend when it opens and stops it when it quits, that Settings > Connection shows whether it is running, names anything that failed, and offers Start and Stop, and that stopping frees the memory the model and voice are holding without closing Hearth while starting brings them back without relaunching. Nothing here is deleted by this task.

The platform-overview shape and its rules. 243-245 puts installation on the install page and names a platform overview that grows an install procedure as how the corpus ended up with two install guides. 246-248 forbids a dated status log. 249-250 moves reference material off the page. 251-252 requires the sections in a fixed order across every client.

The corpus's fullest published treatment of the same controls, written for the other platform. windows.md:96-99 names the pane 'Settings > The house' and lists Start, Stop and Restart, explaining that Restart is start again. windows.md:48-58 states that closing the window minimizes to the tray with the backend still running, that Quit is the explicit stop, and that Quit, Stop and Restart all flush the session first. native-runtime.md:68-71 states the same lifecycle for both platforms, naming the menu bar on macOS.

The recorded plan: the salvage table (196-205) assigning both passages to T6, the redirect rule and inbound-reference list (214-216), the phase table putting T6 in B and the redirects in C (225), the T6 row and draft (841-878), and T16's retirement gate (1195-1216).
